terms.comment: Priscian’s Greek word (σύνταξις). Traupman’s pupil answers how he knows a case: Ā syntaxī, from the syntax (239).

Cicero uses it of the arrangement of words in a sentence (verbōrum cōnstrūctiō et numerus, Or. 37, Lewis & Short); as the grammarian’s term for a construction it is Priscian’s. Cicero’s other phrase is cōnfōrmātiō verbōrum (de Or. 1.151, Lewis & Short).
Traupman offers it as the “pure Latin” word; Lewis & Short gives it of order and arrangement in general (Vitruvius, Pliny), not of words.

phrases.latin: Unde hoc certum est? — Ā syntaxī.
phrases.english: How is that certain? — From the syntax.

ordinatio.html: From ōrdō, which the lexicon writes with a long o; Lewis & Short leaves both words unmarked.

sources: Lewis & Short: syntaxis · Lewis & Short: constructio · Lewis & Short: ordinatio
